sentences.sentence: ## My Ego Sabotaged My Writing
**Illustration by Fresh Idea**
Full manuscript in two months.
That was the goal.
I was on vacation in Mexico, no less, when I checked my email and saw the opportunity.
It was mid-June and the conference was happening near the end of July.
My mind raced with the possibilities: a chance to present my work, network with other writers, maybe even get published.
I knew this conference was my ticket.
My ego, ever the eager participant, jumped in full force.
“You can do this!
You’re talented, you’re smart, you’ve got the fire,” it whispered.
Fueled by this intoxicating confidence, I dove headfirst into the project, determined to churn out a manuscript that would impress everyone.
The problem was, I forgot about the art of writing.
I sacrificed quality for speed, sacrificing nuance for urgency.
My words became hollow shells, devoid of the soul and depth that usually characterized my work.
I wrote late into the night, ignoring the waves crashing on the shore, the call of the exotic birds, the warmth of the Mexican sun.
But the manuscript remained incomplete.
I pushed myself harder, ignoring the nagging feeling in my gut that something was wrong.
The pressure built, feeding the fire of my ego, until it consumed me entirely.
Then came the inevitable crash.
The manuscript was nowhere near ready.
I couldn't face the conference, couldn't bear the thought of presenting something so devoid of meaning.
The rush of failure was compounded by the bitter aftertaste of self-deception.
My ego had tricked me, feeding off my ambition until it left me drained and empty.
I learned a hard lesson that summer in Mexico.
True success isn’t about meeting deadlines or impressing others.
It’s about the pursuit of excellence, the careful crafting of words, the joy of creation.
## What in the World is Shaking Up The Hospitality Industry?
How prepared are you for the revolution?
Once upon a time, not that long ago in the restaurant, food and hospitality industry, the formula for success was pretty simple to grasp.
Following the formula was widely accepted as the guaranteed path to making money:  consistent menus, predictable service, and a focus on physical location.
Brick-and-mortar was king, and the world came to you.
But the kingdom has changed.
Today, the hospitality landscape is shifting faster than a waiter during a rush hour.
The winds of change are blowing, fueled by technology, evolving consumer expectations, and a new breed of entrepreneurial spirit.
The pandemic acted as a catalyst, forcing the industry to accelerate its digital transformation.
Now, ghost kitchens, delivery-only models, and online ordering platforms are not just trends, but the new reality.
Restaurants are leveraging social media for marketing and customer engagement, offering interactive experiences and personalized service through apps.
And it's not just about convenience.
Today's guests are looking for more than just a meal; they want an experience.
They crave authenticity, sustainability, and social responsibility.
They want stories behind their food, transparency in sourcing, and a connection with the community.
This isn't a passing fad.
These are fundamental shifts in the way we consume, interact, and experience hospitality.
The question is not if this revolution will come, but if you'll be ready to embrace it.
Here's the good news: the changes also present incredible opportunities for innovation and growth.
Restaurants can leverage technology to streamline operations, personalize service, and connect with customers on a deeper level.
They can build brands that stand for something, showcasing their commitment to ethical practices and social good.
The time to adapt is now.
The hospitality industry is no longer a static entity.
## Building Back Better: A Collaborative Vision for Vermont's Post-Pandemic Future

As the world awaits the results of COVID-19 vaccine clinical trials, we are simultaneously grappling with the profound and lasting impact this pandemic has had on our lives, our communities, and our economy.
While we yearn for a return to normalcy, this moment demands more than simply going back to how things were.
We have a unique opportunity to build back better, to forge a stronger and more equitable Vermont for all.
This will require a collaborative effort, a shared vision built on the diverse experiences and expertise of Vermonters from all walks of life.
We must gather input from organizations and partners across Vermont, to determine what these groups will be in Vermont.
What are the critical needs that have been amplified by the pandemic?
How can we leverage existing strengths and resources to address them effectively?
The voices of our frontline healthcare workers, educators, small business owners, artists, and non-profit leaders are essential.
Their insights will illuminate the challenges and opportunities we face, guiding us towards solutions that are both practical and transformative.
Imagine a Vermont where:
* **Healthcare access is a right, not a privilege.
** We invest in preventative care, strengthen our mental health infrastructure, and expand telehealth options to reach every corner of the state.
* **Our economy is resilient and inclusive.
** We support small businesses, invest in green energy, and create pathways to good-paying jobs for all Vermonters.
* **Education empowers every child.
** We prioritize early childhood education, support struggling students, and equip all Vermonters with the skills they need to thrive in the 21st century.
This vision requires collective action.
It demands a commitment to open dialogue, transparency, and accountability.
It calls for a willingness to challenge the status quo and embrace bold, innovative solutions.
Let us seize this moment.
## How to Change Your Programming to Achieve the Results You Desire.
If negative thoughts turn into beliefs that determine your behavior, then the opposite holds true.
Positive thoughts and beliefs can lead to positive action.
This means we can reprogram our minds to achieve the results we desire.
While the concept might sound daunting, it doesn't require a complete overhaul of your personality or an intensive therapy program.
You can start today with two simple, yet powerful, techniques:
Replace Self-Doubt with Self-Compassion:**
Instead of engaging in this inner critic's vicious cycle, try replacing those thoughts with self-compassion.
Treat yourself with the same kindness and understanding you'd offer a close friend facing a challenge.
Acknowledge your struggles, offer yourself encouragement, and remember that setbacks are a natural part of the journey.
This shift in mindset creates space for growth and resilience, allowing you to face challenges head-on instead of shrinking away.
Visualize Success with Vivid Detail:**
Imagine yourself achieving your goals.
Don't just vaguely hope for it; visualize the experience with laser focus.
See yourself crossing the finish line, holding that promotion letter, or confidently presenting your ideas.
Feel the emotions that accompany success: the pride, the relief, the joy.
This deliberate practice of visualization strengthens your belief in your ability to succeed, rewiring your brain to anticipate and attract positive outcomes.
These two practices, cultivated with consistency, can dramatically impact your life.

By treating yourself with kindness and envisioning your success with clarity, you'll not only change your internal dialogue but also empower yourself to take the actions necessary to achieve your dreams.
Remember, your mind is a powerful tool, and reprogramming it for success is within your reach.

##  Finding My Voice: Learning to Be My Own Advocate
Zion National Park in Utah.
Picture taken by yours truly.
Learning how to love me through creative writing has proven to be a powerful tool in my life.
My thoughts become more apparent, and it leads me to feel confident on my own behalf.
This newfound self-awareness has empowered me to step into the role of my own advocate – a role that is often challenging, but ultimately rewarding.
Advocacy, at its core, is about standing up for yourself, your needs, and your values.
It's about making your voice heard and ensuring your perspective is considered.
For me, this journey began with introspection.
Writing allowed me to unpack my feelings, identify my strengths and weaknesses, and understand what truly mattered to me.
Once I had a clearer picture of myself, I began to apply this understanding to real-life situations.
It started small: speaking up in meetings, politely but firmly voicing my opinions, and setting boundaries in my personal relationships.
Each time I did this, I felt a sense of accomplishment, a confirmation that my voice deserved to be heard.
This newfound confidence hasn't always been easy.
There have been times when I've been met with resistance or doubt.
But I've learned that true advocacy requires resilience and a willingness to persevere.
It's about knowing your worth and refusing to be silenced.
Being my own advocate has had a profound impact on my life.
I feel more empowered, more in control, and more fulfilled.
It's about taking ownership of my narrative and shaping my own future.
It's a journey, not a destination.
There will always be new challenges and opportunities to advocate for myself.
But with each step I take, I become stronger, more confident, and more capable of living a life that is truly my own.

##  Healthy Relationships: 3 Keys to Manifest a Long Term Love Life Immediately
It’s a bit embarrassing for me that Charice and Johann have witnessed my continuous failures in relationships.
They have listened to my rants and given me compassionate advice in the 6 years I’ve been spilling my relationship woes to them.
"You're too quick to judge," Charice would say, while Johann would chime in with, "Focus on the good, not the bad."
But it took a while for me to truly grasp the power of choosing a calmer, more constructive path.
It took me realizing that happiness in love wasn't about winning a battle, but about creating a safe and loving space to grow.
That’s when I discovered three key principles that have drastically changed my outlook on love.
Let the drama happen around you, not with you.
We live in a world obsessed with drama.
Every social media feed is brimming with relationship scandals and fiery arguments.
It's easy to get swept up in that energy, to project our own insecurities and anxieties onto our partners.
But true love thrives on peace and understanding.
It requires choosing empathy over judgment, communication over accusation.
When the drama comes knocking, take a step back.
Breathe.
Listen to understand, not to respond.
Cultivate your own inner garden before tending to someone else’s.
We can’t expect to pour love into another person if our own cup is empty.
Invest in yourself.
Learn to love who you are, flaws and all.
Nurture your passions, pursue your dreams, and prioritize your mental and emotional well-being.
When you are secure and fulfilled, you will attract a partner who reflects that same sense of self-love and growth.
##  The Echoes of Childhood: Why Investing in Children is Investing in a Better Future
"This in simple words means that the traits of childhood continue in manhood.
In other words, if we want to have better men, we must first have better children.

If we pay no attention to the child, he grows into a worthless youth and..."  This quote, echoing the philosophical wisdom "The Child is the Father of the Man," rings as true today as it did centuries ago.
It serves as a stark reminder that the seeds of our future society are sown in the tender years of childhood.
While seemingly obvious, this concept often gets lost amidst the hustle and bustle of adult life.
We focus on immediate concerns, neglecting the long-term impact of how we nurture our children.
But the truth is, neglecting childhood development is a dangerous gamble.
The traits, values, and behaviors instilled in a child become the foundation upon which their adulthood is built.
Imagine a child who is consistently exposed to negativity, aggression, or a lack of emotional support.
What are the chances that they will blossom into a kind, responsible, and empathetic adult?
Conversely, a child raised in an environment of love, security, and encouragement is far more likely to develop into a well-rounded, contributing member of society.
So, what does this mean for us?
It means prioritizing the well-being and development of our children.
It means investing in quality education, accessible healthcare, and nurturing relationships.
It means creating a society that values childhood and recognizes its profound impact on the future.
We cannot afford to view children as mere bystanders in the grand scheme of things.
They are not mini-adults; they are individuals in their own right, deserving of respect, care, and support.
